item.title: Big Data File Formats
item.description:
Big-data file formats trade off storage efficiency, schema evolution, and query speed. The best choice depends on whether the workload mostly scans records, reads a few columns across many rows, or exchanges events between systems.

Row-Oriented Formats #

Row-oriented formats place the fields of one record together. Avro is a common example. It is useful for streaming, event interchange, and write-heavy workloads because reading a complete record is efficient. Avro stores its writer schema with the data and has explicit schema-resolution rules that support compatible evolution.

item.title: Apache Flink and Kafka Integration
item.description:
Apache Flink is a distributed processing engine for stateful computations over bounded and unbounded data streams. It can consume events as they arrive, maintain application state, use event time, recover from failures, and continuously publish results.

Apache Kafka is a distributed event-streaming platform. Producers append records to partitioned topics, Kafka retains those records, and consumers read them at their own pace. Kafka is commonly the durable transport layer in a streaming architecture, while Flink performs the computation:
